claims.text: The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys, including refractory HEAs, in high-temperature solid and liquid states near melting.
Conventional EAM reference potentials are unable to represent the wide range of atomic configurations encountered in the ab initio liquid.
Replacing an EAM reference with an MLIP trained on representative ab initio configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
The MLIP should be trained on diverse ab initio configurations from both liquid and near-melting solid states.
A neural-network potential or Gaussian approximation potential can be used as the MLIP framework.
The resulting MLIP can replace the EAM reference within the TOR-TILD thermodynamic-integration scheme.
The intervention is applicable to alloys containing five or more elements.
The proposed temperature range is approximately within ±50 K of the alloy melting point.
Liquid and high-temperature solid HEAs exhibit a broad configuration space.
An adequately trained MLIP can emulate the ab initio energy landscape across a wider range of local atomic environments than the more limited EAM functional form.
Training on a large ensemble of ab initio local configurations enables the MLIP to capture complex interatomic interactions and statistical fluctuations in the ab initio liquid.
Improved representation of liquid interactions and fluctuations produces better phase-space overlap.
Better phase-space overlap reduces mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The MLIP reference will improve thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 25–30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Using the MLIP reference will yield free-energy estimates closer to direct ab initio predictions.
The anticipated improvement requires a sufficiently diverse training set that covers nearly all relevant high-temperature configurations.
Incomplete training coverage or extreme compositional or configurational complexity may eliminate the improvement.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on training-data quality and breadth, alloy composition, and temperature.
The benchmark should compare EAM-reference and MLIP-reference TOR-TILD calculations for the same alloy and configurations against a direct ab initio free-energy calculation.
Failure to reduce path mismatch by at least approximately 20–25%, or failure to move the free energy significantly closer to the ab initio benchmark, falsifies the hypothesis.
